reviewDomains.summary: The production delta does not alter the established signed permit/ACK/receipt wire formats or canonical protocol parsers. The new activation boundary consumes the already-verified journaled permit and uses strict JSON decoding for its local config/approval inputs; exact approval SHA-256 is rebound before network I/O.

No signature algorithm, key-purpose binding or key material format is changed. Production execution reuses runtime.Exchange/Recover and the existing Ed25519 AND ML-DSA-65 permit/ACK/receipt verification chain; approval v2 forbids classical-only mode.

The isolated production ingress uses the already-reviewed TLS 1.3/X25519MLKEM768 configuration with mandatory client certificate verification. Node execution loads explicit roots/client identity and reuses strict mutual-PQ Dial/Exchange; redirects, proxy fallback and classical fallback remain absent.

Production runs the existing signer as an isolated read-only service with dedicated UDS and separately mounted key directory; C2-C connects only through the signer socket. Key-file ownership/mode checks remain inside the signer and fail closed. Host provisioning of signer keys remains an operator trust boundary.

The production delta does not modify existing durable XSP-v2 tables, migrations, C2-C transaction logic, signer receipt logic or origin ACK/recovery implementation. The only new PostgreSQL provisioning file creates a least-privilege permit-signer role and contains no CREATE/ALTER/DROP/TRUNCATE TABLE operation.

No qualified Agent state, keyring sealed-state or strict transport implementation is modified. The new one-shot activation binary reads existing durable active state and refuses an approval whose expected candidate differs from the active epoch/key IDs. Crash durability and snapshot anti-rollback CI remain green on the production Node target.

Existing recovery-floor/off-host logic is unchanged and #138 evidence is carried forward only after exact protected-path diff checks. Provider-managed KVM storage remains an accepted external durability trust boundary and physical power loss is not claimed.

The production activation path explicitly retains XMESH1 and contains no key retirement operation. Existing owner-authorized retirement protocol and anti-resurrection state are unchanged and remain a separate later action.

Existing parser fuzz and external ML-DSA-65 vector evidence remains applicable because core protocol/crypto parsers are unchanged. The new local activation JSON parser is bounded and unknown-field rejecting but is not separately fuzz-certified; this is an informational assurance limitation rather than a release blocker.

The new strict-PQ production services are under an explicit Compose profile and are absent from default startup. Stack readiness records strictPQEnabled=false; only a verified Node receipt result can produce the final durable activation record. Existing observability paths are unchanged.
evidence: production runtime CI merged Compose validation

reviewDomains.summary: The missing production execution layer is now explicit: approval-bound launcher starts isolated signer/C2-C/origin/ingress, Node one-shot executor re-binds approval/source/artifact/scope/window/durable state before strict-PQ exchange, finalization requires verified receipt evidence, and rollback is manual and preserves Node state/XMESH1. No automatic/classical-only fallback exists. Existing standalone services retain their historical staging-only compatibility token internally; production authorization is the outer root-owned approval launcher and bounded Node approval.
evidence: Nexus PR #186 production runtime CI success

findings.title: KVM provider durability remains an external trust boundary
findings.disposition: Release owner continues to accept provider-managed durable-flush semantics for the KVM deployment class without claiming host/controller/PLP physical qualification.

findings.title: Security assurance remains AI-assisted/internal rather than organizationally independent
findings.disposition: Release owner explicitly accepts the reduced organizational-independence assurance while retaining technical fail-closed gates, exact-candidate canary and bounded execution.

findings.title: Standalone signer/C2-C/origin binaries retain historical staging-only compatibility tokens
findings.disposition: The tokens are not treated as production authorization. Production exposure is controlled by the default-off Compose profile, root-only approval launcher, exact approval verification and Node-side approval/artifact/scope/window checks. Direct Docker/root administration remains an operator trust boundary.

signoff.statement: AI-assisted internal delta review of the production-capable XSP-v2 target found no unresolved Critical, High, Medium or Low release-blocking vulnerability. Core cryptography, durable key state, ACK/receipt transactionality and strict transport remain unchanged; the new production execution layer is bounded, default-off, approval-bound and has no automatic/classical fallback.

releaseOwnerRiskAcceptance.statement: Release owner accepts the AI-assisted internal assurance model, the documented KVM provider-storage trust boundary, and the root/operator administration boundary of the isolated production services. This acceptance does not waive durability carry-forward verification, exact-target final canary, rollout/rollback review, bounded approval, verified receipt finalization, no-fallback policy, or separate XMESH1 retirement.
